=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary observations

**1. The "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing should be disregarded.** The preamble asserts these positions were agreed by both deal teams and "are not intended to be re-opened". Nothing in our instructions confirms that. Please check with the Wattlebridge principals whether *any* of these positions were actually agreed; if not, respond that the Buyer does not accept the characterisation and reserves all positions. Even if some were discussed, a liability cap is never "agreed" in isolation from the warranty package, disclosure standard, knowledge qualifier and indemnities – and those have moved against us here.

**2. The "market context" paragraph is advocacy, not advice.** Individual numbers (20% cap, 1% basket, 18 months) are each within a defensible range for a deal of this size. The problem is the *combination*: a low cap, deductible basket, short period, constructive-knowledge bar, blanket data-room disclosure, and extension of all limitations to every class of claim. Taken together, the package would leave the Buyer with almost no practical recourse.

**3. The Disclosure Letter is more candid than the Seller Update.** The Update describes Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and the bonuses as "addressed" or "not material"; the Disclosure Letter admits that none of them is resolved. Read the two together and the Update's reassurances fall away.

---

## Material issues

### A. Liability architecture (Clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5)

| Seller position | Problem for Buyer | Push back |
|---|---|---|
| **12.1** General cap 20% (AUD 4.8m) | Low-end, and here it is being used as the cap for *everything* (see 12.3/13 and 9.3/12.8/20.5). | Acceptable only if ring-fenced to general business warranties. Push for 30–50% absent W&I insurance; if the Seller insists on 20%, trade for a 10% escrow/retention (see F below) and carve-outs. |
| **12.2** De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k **excess-only** | A deductible basket means the first AUD 250k of loss is simply lost. Combined with a 25k de minimis, many SaaS-type claims (individual customer, contract, employee issues) never count. | Basket should be **tipping** (first-dollar recovery once exceeded). De minimis 10–15k. Related claims arising from the same facts to aggregate (note the Sandbar "three × 110k" structure – the Seller is already splitting items). |
| **12.3** 18 months; **13** "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | The second sentence is the real issue: it sweeps fundamental, tax, specific indemnities and leakage/price-adjustment claims into the 18-month/20%/basket regime by default. | Reject the default rule. 24 months for general warranties (two audit cycles). Tax: 7 years / expiry of ATO amendment periods. Title/capacity: 7 years or unlimited. Specific indemnities: their own longer periods. |
| **Fundamental / Title** subject to general caps "for administrative simplicity" | Non-negotiable. If title to the shares fails, recovery limited to 20% of price is absurd. | Title, capacity, authority (and ideally IP ownership) capped at **100% of price**, outside basket/de minimis, long-stop 7 years+. |
| **9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5** limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Would purport to limit fraud, wilful concealment, tax indemnity, specific indemnities, W&I-related claims and completion-accounts/leakage adjustments. Exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language can also be read to exclude misleading-or-deceptive-conduct claims (ACL s 18 cannot be contracted out of, but the drafting signals the intent). | Express carve-outs for fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct; tax indemnity; specific indemnities; price-adjustment/leakage mechanics; equitable and injunctive relief. Non-reliance limited to statements *outside* the SPA, with an express fraud carve-out. |
| **8.3** No claim for matters the Buyer/advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable" from data room or public records | This is a constructive-knowledge bar. Combined with Sched 7 general disclosure, it effectively converts every warranty into "unless it was somewhere in 12 data-room folders or on a public register". It also undermines any W&I policy (insurers will not accept it). | Delete. Fall-back: actual knowledge of a short named list of deal team individuals, and only matters "fairly disclosed" in the Disclosure Letter. No imputation of advisers' knowledge. |
| **Sched 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2** general disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" | Blanket disclosure of thousands of pages and open-ended public records is not disclosure at all. Public-record disclosure in particular (ASIC, PPSR, court lists, IP registers) is a trap. | Disclosure standard: "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter". Data-room disclosure only against specific warranties with cross-references, and only to the frozen index (22 Sept 2026). Delete public-records disclosure, or confine it to named searches actually done and attached. |

### B. Debt-free / cash-free is not being delivered

**Riverlark facility (AUD ~3.2m, Clause 2/7).** The Seller proposes a release "following Completion". That is inconsistent with the agreed debt-free basis and with DD-003 (change-of-control clause 8.1 – Completion will likely trigger an event of default). Required:
- Payout letter from Riverlark before Completion; repayment at Completion out of the purchase price via the funds flow (direction to pay).
- Deed of release and PPSR discharge (and release of any share/all-asset security and guarantees) delivered **at** Completion as a completion deliverable, not afterwards.
- If any security cannot be discharged on the day, retention of the equivalent amount.
- Confirm whether Riverlark holds security over the *shares* – this also goes to title (see E).

**DD-005 closing bonuses (AUD 420k).** The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" yet they are not in the funds flow. They are a Company liability triggered by Completion and will be paid by the Company (i.e. us) post-Completion, plus superannuation, payroll tax and possibly leave accruals (the Disclosure Letter expressly does not address on-costs – assume ~15–20% on top). Required: treat as Transaction Expenses/Debt deducted from the price, grossed-up for on-costs, or paid by the Seller through the funds flow before Completion with evidence. Also check whether the "continued employment" conditions create retention-payment obligations extending into our ownership.

**Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k = 330k).** The Seller labels them "ordinary course". The Disclosure Letter will not say whether they are accrued, unavoidable or terminable, and DD-008/DD-011 need to be read together – strongly suggesting a single commitment split into three to stay under thresholds. Required: diligence the timing; if committed pre-Completion but payable post, include in Debt / working-capital adjustment or obtain a specific indemnity; apply the aggregation rule in 12.2.

**Ironquay open fee (AUD 180k)** – also an unpaid pre-Completion liability (see C).

### C. Intellectual property – Ironquay (Clause 11.1, DD-004, DD-010)

Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to SOW3 Project Materials does **not** pass until every SOW3 fee is paid. AUD 180k is open and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. Until paid, Ironquay owns that code. An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" compensates only the 180k – not loss of ownership of (potentially core) product IP, injunctive risk or customer impact.

Push for:
- Condition precedent / completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment **and** a confirmatory assignment (and moral-rights consents) from Ironquay in agreed form.
- Diligence what SOW3 covers – if it is in the production codebase this is a title-to-assets point, not a trade creditor point.
- IP ownership warranties treated as fundamental (100% cap, long period) and a specific uncapped (or price-capped) indemnity for any third-party claim over Project Materials.

### D. Conditions and consents

**Bluefen (Clause 3/6.3; DD-002).** ~30% of FY26 revenue. Change-of-control consent under cl 11.2 is subject to conditions under cl 11.3; no consent is in the data room. "Reasonable endeavours" and treating the CP as satisfied "on delivery of written consent" are inadequate – a conditional consent could be delivered on the day with the 11.3 conditions (price concessions, term changes, guarantees) unmet.

Push for: CP satisfied only on unconditional written consent in a form approved by the Buyer (or with all 11.3 conditions satisfied/waived at the Seller's cost); "all reasonable endeavours"; Buyer to be party to the approach to Bluefen; right to walk or renegotiate price if consent not obtained by a long-stop date; consider an earn-out/retention tied to Bluefen revenue retention for 12 months post-Completion.

**Mossvale (DD-009).** Assignment restriction only; the Seller says no consent needed on a share sale. Confirm the clause has no change-of-control limb and that nothing in the group structure causes an assignment. If uncertain, notify-and-confirm pre-Completion.

**Office lease (DD-007).** Notification obligation – ensure the notice is given pre-Completion as a Seller covenant and that the lease does not treat non-notification as default.

### E. Title verification

The Seller relies solely on the Company's own share register (DD-012) and expressly disclaims that the Buyer has verified. We must do our own: ASIC company extract, historical share transfers and any option/convertible instruments (venture-backed company – check for SAFEs, ESOP, convertible notes, preference shares), PPSR search over the shares and over Harbourglass, Riverlark security documents. Completion deliverables: executed transfers, share certificates (or cancellation), board resolution approving transfer and registration, register updated at Completion, resignations. Title warranty must be unqualified and at 100% cap (see A).

### F. Privacy incident (DD-006; Clause 4.6 / Sched 6)

The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". ~1,240 individuals' personal information sent to an unintended external recipient is a potential *eligible data breach* under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme. The Company must complete a reasonable assessment within 30 days of becoming aware and notify OAIC and affected individuals if serious harm is likely. The Disclosure Letter confirms that scope, access and notification are all unresolved.

Push for: pre-Completion covenant to complete the assessment and share the report; Buyer approval of any notification decision; specific indemnity (outside cap/basket, 3–6 years) for regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims and any Bluefen/other customer contract consequences flowing from DD-006. Check customer contracts (especially Bluefen) for data-incident notification obligations that may already have been triggered.

### G. Tax

"Settled under the general regime" means tax exposures capped at 20%, basket applies, and time-barred at 18 months – before the ATO's standard amendment period has even run. Require a standard separate tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, grossed-up, no basket, 100% cap or uncapped, period aligned to amendment periods), plus the usual tax covenants on pre-Completion returns. Also confirm R&D tax incentive claims and payroll tax on contractors – common SaaS exposures.

### H. Seller covenant strength

Harbourglass Ventures is a venture entity. Sale proceeds may be distributed to investors shortly after Completion, leaving an empty counterparty for any claim. The limitations package only matters if the Seller can pay. Require: escrow/retention (suggest 10% of price for the general warranty period, longer tranche for the specific indemnities), a parent/fund guarantee, or a covenant to maintain net assets at or above the cap for the claims period.

---

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Do not accept the "FINAL" framing.** Confirm internally what (if anything) was agreed; reply that the full package is open and that the Buyer's mark-up follows.
2. **Rebuild the limitations schedule:** general warranties 24 months, cap 30–50% (or 20% + 10% escrow); tipping basket; fundamental/title/IP-ownership and tax at 100% of price with 7-year periods; specific indemnities outside caps/basket; carve-outs for fraud, tax indemnity, leakage/price adjustments. Delete the "limitations apply to all Claims" default and the "all Claims of any nature" language in 9.3/12.8/20.5.
3. **Delete Clause 8.3** (buyer knowledge) or confine to actual knowledge of named individuals of matters fairly disclosed.
4. **Replace general disclosure** with a "fairly disclosed" standard, specific cross-referenced disclosures only, no open-ended public-records disclosure.
5. **Enforce debt-free/cash-free:** Riverlark repaid and released *at* Completion through the funds flow; DD-005 bonuses (+ on-costs) and Ironquay AUD 180k deducted from price; Sandbar renewals diligenced and either adjusted or indemnified; aggregation of related claims.
6. **Bluefen as a hard CP** – unconditional consent in agreed form, 11.3 conditions satisfied at Seller's cost, walk/price-adjustment right, consider revenue-based retention.
7. **Ironquay:** payment and confirmatory assignment as CP; IP warranties fundamental; specific indemnity beyond the fee amount.
8. **DD-006:** complete NDB assessment pre-Completion, Buyer control of notification, specific indemnity.
9. **Tax:** separate tax indemnity on market terms, not the general regime.
10. **Title:** independent ASIC/PPSR verification, check for options/convertibles/preference shares, full completion deliverables.
11. **Covenant strength:** escrow/retention or guarantee from the Harbourglass fund/parent.
12. **Minor:** Mossvale confirmation; office-lease notice as Seller covenant; related-claims aggregation; Disclosure Letter frozen to the 22 Sept 2026 index with no further "general" updates.

Happy to turn this into a formal issues list / SPA mark-up or a response letter to Seller's counsel on request.

Require a standard separate tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, grossed-up, no basket, 100% cap or uncapped, period aligned to amendment periods), plus the usual tax covenants on pre-Completion returns. Also confirm R&D tax incentive claims and payroll tax on contractors – common SaaS exposures.

### H. Seller covenant strength

Harbourglass Ventures is a venture entity. Sale proceeds may be distributed to investors shortly after Completion, leaving an empty counterparty for any claim. The limitations package only matters if the Seller can pay. Require: escrow/retention (suggest 10% of price for the general warranty period, longer tranche for the specific indemnities), a parent/fund guarantee, or a covenant to maintain net assets at or above the cap for the claims period.
